title: Telling stories & real conversation
goal: Tell a simple story, report what others said, describe people and things with relative clauses, and sound natural with fillers and idioms.
intro:
Real Telugu conversation is full of little words that glue it together: *అంటే* (I mean), *మరి* (so, well), *అసలు* (actually), *కదా* (isn't it?), *ఏమో* (who knows). This final unit gives you those, plus the two structures you need for storytelling: **relative clauses** (the man *who came*) and **reported speech** (he said *that*...).

Telugu stories traditionally begin with *ఒకప్పుడు...* ('once upon a time'), and the most loved trickster of all is the poet **Tenali Ramakrishna**.

vocab.en: once upon a time; in the past

vocab.note: అన్నాడు (he said), అంది (she said), అంటారు (they say)

vocab.en: that is, I mean; if one says
well, so, and then; then what about
well then; never mind; how about
vocab.note: పోనీలే = never mind, let it go.

phrases.en: So what shall we do now?
Don't try to fool me! (lit. don't put a flower in my ear)

phrases.native: ఒకప్పుడు ఒక ఊళ్ళో ఒక రాజు ఉండేవాడు.
phrases.roman: okappuḍu oka ūḷḷō oka rāju uṇḍēvāḍu.
phrases.en: Once upon a time, in a certain town, there lived a king.
Sour grapes. (lit. the grapes you can't reach are sour)

grammar.title: Relative clauses: the man who came
grammar.body:
Telugu has no 'who/which/that'. Instead, the verb becomes an **adjective-like participle** placed **before** the noun:
• past **-ఇన** (-ina): *వచ్చిన అబ్బాయి* (the boy who came), *నేను చదివిన పుస్తకం* (the book I read)
• non-past **-ఏ** (-ē): *వచ్చే బస్సు* (the bus that comes / will come), *తెలుగు మాట్లాడే వాళ్ళు* (people who speak Telugu)
• negative **-అని** (-ani): *రాని వాళ్ళు* (those who don't come)

Add **-వాడు / -వాళ్ళు / -ది** to make 'the one who': *చేసేవాళ్ళు* (those who do), *మీరు చెప్పింది* (what you said).

The past habitual 'used to' is the non-past participle + **-వాడు / -ది / -వాళ్ళు**: *ఉండేవాడు* (he used to live), *పారిపోయేది* (it used to run away).

examples.en: The boy who came yesterday is my younger brother.
The book I read is very good.
Is this the bus that goes to Hyderabad?
Few foreigners speak Telugu. (lit. Telugu-speaking foreigners are few)

grammar.title: Reported speech: అని and -మని
grammar.body:
Telugu usually keeps the speaker's **original words**, closed with **అని**, before a verb of saying: *"రేపు వస్తాను" అని అన్నాడు* = he said, 'I'll come tomorrow' = he said he'd come tomorrow. Questions are reported the same way with **అడుగు** (ask).

**Reported commands** use **-మని** on the verb: *రమ్మని చెప్పారు* (they told [me] to come), *వెళ్ళమని అన్నారు* (they said to go).

**Hearsay** ('apparently, they say') is the suffix **-అట** (-aṭa) on the verb, as in Unit 13.

examples.native: నువ్వు ఎక్కడ ఉన్నావు అని అమ్మ అడిగింది.
examples.roman: nuvvu ekkaḍa unnāvu ani amma aḍigindi.

examples.en: They told me to come early.
What did he say? He said 'nothing'.

grammar.title: Fillers and proverbs
grammar.body:
Sprinkle these and you'll sound much more natural:
**అంటే...** (I mean...) · **మరి** (so / well / and what about...) · **అసలు** (actually; *అసలు రాలేదు*, didn't come at all) · **కదా** (right?) · **ఏమో** (who knows) · **అబ్బా!** (wow / ugh) · **హమ్మయ్య!** (phew) · **పోనీలే** (never mind) · **అంతే** (that's all).

Telugu is rich in proverbs (*సామెతలు*), used constantly in conversation:
*ఆలస్యం అమృతం విషం* (delay turns nectar into poison) · *కోటి విద్యలు కూటి కొరకే* (all the world's skills are for a meal = we all work to eat) · *ఇంట గెలిచి రచ్చ గెలువు* (win at home first, then in public) · *అందని ద్రాక్ష పుల్లన* (sour grapes).

examples.en: I mean, what I'm saying is...
Delay turns nectar into poison. (Don't put it off.)
All skills are for earning one's bread.

dialogue.title: Tenali Ramakrishna's cat
dialogue.setting: Ammamma (grandmother) tells her grandson Chintu a Tenali Ramakrishna story at bedtime.

lines.speaker: Chintu
lines.en: Grandma, won't you tell me a story?

lines.speaker: Ammamma
lines.native: సరే విను. ఒకప్పుడు విజయనగరంలో తెనాలి రామకృష్ణుడు అనే కవి ఉండేవాడు.
lines.roman: sarē vinu. okappuḍu vijayanagaramlō tenāli rāmakruṣṇuḍu anē kavi uṇḍēvāḍu.
lines.en: All right, listen. Once upon a time in Vijayanagara there lived a poet called Tenali Ramakrishna.

lines.speaker: Ammamma
lines.native: ఒకరోజు రాజు అందరికీ ఒక పిల్లిని, ఒక ఆవుని ఇచ్చాడు. పిల్లికి రోజూ పాలు పోయండి అని చెప్పాడు.
lines.roman: okarōju rāju andarikī oka pillini, oka āvuni ichchāḍu. pilliki rōjū pālu pōyaṇḍi ani cheppāḍu.
lines.en: One day the king gave everyone a cat and a cow. He told them to give the cat milk every day.

lines.speaker: Ammamma
lines.native: రామకృష్ణుడు మొదటి రోజే పిల్లికి బాగా వేడి పాలు పెట్టాడు. పిల్లి నోరు కాలింది. అప్పటి నుంచి అది పాలు చూస్తే పారిపోయేది.
lines.roman: rāmakruṣṇuḍu modaṭi rōjē pilliki bāgā vēḍi pālu peṭṭāḍu. pilli nōru kālindi. appaṭi nunchi adi pālu chūstē pāripōyēdi.
lines.en: On the very first day Ramakrishna gave the cat really hot milk. The cat burnt its mouth. From then on, whenever it saw milk, it would run away.

lines.speaker: Chintu
lines.native: అయ్యో పాపం పిల్లి! మరి ఆవు పాలు?
lines.roman: ayyō pāpam pilli! mari āvu pālu?
lines.en: Oh, poor cat! And the cow's milk?

lines.speaker: Ammamma
lines.native: ఆ పాలన్నీ రామకృష్ణుడే తాగాడు! చివరికి అందరి పిల్లులు లావుగా ఉన్నాయి, రామకృష్ణుడి పిల్లి మాత్రం సన్నగా ఉంది.
lines.roman: ā pālannī rāmakruṣṇuḍē tāgāḍu! chivariki andari pillulu lāvugā unnāyi, rāmakruṣṇuḍi pilli mātram sannagā undi.
lines.en: Ramakrishna drank all that milk himself! In the end everyone's cats were fat, but Ramakrishna's cat was thin.

lines.speaker: Chintu
lines.en: Did the king get angry then?

lines.speaker: Ammamma
lines.native: వచ్చింది. కానీ రామకృష్ణుడు పిల్లి ముందు పాలు పెట్టాడు. పిల్లి పారిపోయింది! చూడండి మహారాజా, దీనికి పాలు ఇష్టం లేదట అన్నాడు.
lines.roman: vachchindi. kānī rāmakruṣṇuḍu pilli mundu pālu peṭṭāḍu. pilli pāripōyindi! chūḍaṇḍi mahārājā, dīniki pālu iṣṭam lēdaṭa annāḍu.
lines.en: He did. But Ramakrishna put milk in front of the cat, and the cat ran away! 'Look, Your Majesty, it seems it doesn't like milk,' he said.

lines.speaker: Ammamma
lines.native: అందుకే అతని కథలు ఇప్పటికీ అందరూ చెప్పుకుంటారు. ఇక పడుకో!
lines.roman: andukē atani kathalu ippaṭikī andarū cheppukuṇṭāru. ika paḍukō!
lines.en: That's why everyone still tells his stories. Now go to sleep!

culture: Tenali Ramakrishna was a 16th-century poet at the court of Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara, and his witty tales are told to every Telugu child. Telugu also has a proud literary tradition going back a thousand years, from Nannaya's *Mahabharata* to the poet-saint Annamayya and the composer Tyagaraja, whose Carnatic songs are in Telugu. Mastering a few proverbs and the fillers in this unit is the quickest way to make Telugu speakers smile and say *అరే, మీరు బాగా తెలుగు మాట్లాడుతున్నారే!* ('Hey, you speak Telugu really well!').
